context: Ravi applies for a museum visitor-services job. The practical exercise asks candidates to write directions for a visitor who has never used the ticket machine. The panel receives a short observation from the trial. One reviewer asks whether a visitor could complete the task. The other is interested in how Ravi learned to write.
rule: Clear instructions means a first-time visitor can collect a ticket without help. The exercise has one published criterion. The application materials do not request a particular degree.
walk: Both reviewers read the same trial. A asks whether the visitor succeeded unaided, exactly the test the panel published. B moves from the visitor’s performance to Ravi’s formal qualification. Publishing a degree requirement would change the exercise. The file gives no basis for assuming that Ravi has, or lacks, that degree.
brief: What is the visitor trial meant to establish?
Which question introduces a new standard?
Could the visitor collect the ticket?
Did the observer supply a hint?
Does Ravi hold a technical-writing degree?
A degree is an additional requirement.
